mem.title: In-memory coordinator state
mem.overview: Ephemeral Go objects inside one coordinator process. They make routing, streaming, caching, throttling, and concurrent coordination fast; they are not a second database.
mem.construction: Usually constructed in api.NewServer or registry.New, then shared by HTTP handlers, provider WebSocket loops, and background controllers.
mem.walk: Maps and slices are looked up or iterated under mutexes; hot counters use atomics; producer/consumer handoffs use bounded channels. Each construct page names the actual type and guard.
mem.durability: Most state starts empty after restart. A few caches are deliberately re-seeded from PostgreSQL, but live sockets, queues, pending requests, EWMAs, and rate-limit buckets cannot be restored.

pg.title: PostgreSQL durable state
pg.overview: Named SQL tables in the coordinator’s production store. Each node is a durable relation, not an in-process object.
pg.construction: Schema creation and migrations live in coordinator/store/postgres.go and coordinator/store/migrations. Store methods hide SQL from handlers.
pg.walk: Handlers call typed Store methods that SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, UPSERT, or transact. R/W/RW badges summarize the API namespace’s access, not PostgreSQL lock modes.
pg.durability: Rows survive coordinator restarts and are the source of truth for identities, billing, releases, model registry, and historical telemetry.

ext.title: External systems
ext.overview: A network or platform boundary outside the coordinator process: SaaS APIs, Apple services, model/object hosting, geo lookup, or consumer-provided HTTPS media.
ext.construction: Clients are configured from deployment environment and use HTTP/APNs/vendor protocols. A node means “the handler crosses this boundary,” not that the service lives in coordinator memory.
ext.walk: CALL edges identify endpoints that invoke, validate data from, redirect to, or return URLs for that system. Failure behavior differs by node and is described on its page.
ext.durability: The external system owns its own lifecycle and storage; the coordinator keeps only bounded client/cache state.

mdm.title: MicroMDM device-management plane
mdm.overview: MicroMDM is a separate Apple MDM server process packaged beside the coordinator. It enrolls provider Macs and supplies independent device posture evidence.
mdm.construction: The deployment start script launches MicroMDM with persistent /data/micromdm state. coordinator/mdm is an HTTP client and response correlator, not the MDM server itself.
mdm.walk: The coordinator looks up enrolled devices, sends SecurityInfo or raw attestation commands, triggers APNs check-in, and receives webhook responses matched by command UUID.
mdm.durability: MicroMDM persists enrollment/device state. In-process command waiters are temporary and are lost on coordinator restart.

prompt.title: Prompt-contract sidecar
prompt.overview: A child process reached through a Unix-domain HTTP socket. It renders/tokenizes prompts, computes contract/cache boundaries, and manages optimizer artifacts without putting that work in the coordinator hot path.
prompt.construction: promptcontract.Supervisor starts and restarts the child; the client uses /run/darkbloom/promptsidecar.sock with separate plan, health, and control transports.
prompt.walk: The coordinator calls health, plan, and preload endpoints; the supervisor polls readiness/RSS and restarts unhealthy children; the artifact provisioner fetches manifests/objects to bounded SSD cache.
prompt.durability: The child is replaceable. Contract/artifact cache may survive on configured SSD, while process health and in-flight calls do not.

provider.title: Provider protocol boundary
provider.overview: The persistent WebSocket control/data protocol between the Go coordinator and each Swift provider node at /ws/provider.
provider.construction: A provider opens WSS, sends Register, then heartbeats and attestation/model/inference frames. The coordinator creates one live Registry.Provider and bounded two-lane writer.
provider.walk: Coordinator→provider frames dispatch/cancel inference and manage models/trust. Provider→coordinator frames report acceptance, chunks, terminal usage, heartbeats, model state, and attestation evidence.
provider.durability: The socket and live Provider object end on disconnect. The node reconnects and registers again; only selected identity/reputation/trust evidence is durable.

ext.apple.overview: Apple services provide APNs delivery and device/MDM attestation infrastructure.
ext.apple.represents: APNs pushes that wake enrolled Macs plus Apple-backed certificate/attestation evidence.
ext.apple.construction: APNs/MDM clients use deployment certificates/keys and device identities.
ext.apple.access: Trust verification triggers pushes/commands and validates returned evidence; unavailable verification fails or degrades according to trust policy, never silently fabricates proof.
ext.apple.concurrency: Concurrency is owned by the typed client/store or by the coordinator object named here; request handlers do not mutate an unguarded global value.
ext.apple.lifecycle: Apple and device enrollment own the external lifecycle.
ext.apple.restart: See the category durability rule; durable truth is reloaded, external/protocol state is re-established.

ext.datadog.represents: DogStatsD metrics, logs intake, traces, and operational events.
ext.datadog.construction: A datadog.Client and telemetry.Emitter are optional deployment-configured clients.
ext.datadog.access: Coordinator emits best-effort; failures are logged and do not block inference.
ext.datadog.concurrency: Concurrency is owned by the typed client/store or by the coordinator object named here; request handlers do not mutate an unguarded global value.
ext.datadog.lifecycle: Datadog retains remote telemetry; local counters reset.

ext.geo.construction: providerGeoResolver is configured at Server creation.

ext.media.construction: mediafetch.Resolver applies scheme, DNS/IP, redirect, port, timeout, concurrency, and byte-budget policy.
ext.media.access: Every URL is resolved and checked against SSRF policy; any fetch error cancels the batch and the request fails before provider dispatch.

ext.privy.represents: ES256 user JWT verification plus REST calls for first-login user details and admin email OTP flows.
ext.privy.construction: auth.PrivyAuthenticator is configured with the Privy app ID and verification key.
ext.privy.access: JWTs are verified locally; selected user/OTP operations call Privy HTTPS APIs. Identity-dependent requests fail closed when verification cannot complete.
ext.privy.concurrency: Concurrency is owned by the typed client/store or by the coordinator object named here; request handlers do not mutate an unguarded global value.

ext.r2.construction: CI publishes with R2 credentials; the coordinator stores/returns URLs and the artifact provisioner fetches allowed objects.
ext.r2.access: Most consumer catalog calls return metadata/URLs rather than proxying model bytes; artifact provisioning performs bounded downloads.

ext.stripe.construction: billing Stripe clients use secret deployment credentials; webhook handlers verify Stripe signatures.
ext.stripe.access: Billing endpoints call Stripe REST; webhooks drive durable billing state. Invalid signatures fail closed; vendor failures return billing errors without bypassing ledger checks.

ext.stripe.lifecycle: Stripe owns payment objects; coordinator tables mirror/reconcile application state.

mem.alias_lock.overview: A cross-endpoint transaction lock for model-alias changes.
mem.alias_lock.represents: One Server-level mutex, not a data collection: it protects the validate → persist → registry-resync critical section shared by alias create/update/delete endpoints.
mem.alias_lock.access: Every alias mutation endpoint locks before reading dependent alias/catalog state, writing PostgreSQL, and fanning out desired model state.
mem.alias_lock.concurrency: A plain mutex deliberately serializes rare administrative mutations; routing reads use registry snapshots and do not take this lock.
mem.alias_lock.lifecycle: Process lifetime, held only for one mutation critical section.
mem.alias_lock.restart: The lock resets; alias truth is reloaded from PostgreSQL.

mem.api_key_cache.overview: The hot-path authentication cache for customer API keys, including negative lookups.
mem.api_key_cache.represents: Raw-token lookup keys map to an APIKey record (or nil for known-invalid), cached time, and a generation number.
mem.api_key_cache.construction: Server creates map[string]apiKeyCacheEntry; TTL is 60 seconds and maximum size is 1,000.
mem.api_key_cache.access: Authentication reads under RLock and validates TTL/generation; misses query PostgreSQL then fill. Any create/delete/update bumps one generation to invalidate the whole logical cache.
mem.api_key_cache.concurrency: apiKeyCacheMu guards the map; generation closes the stale-read race between concurrent authentication and key mutation HTTP handlers.
mem.api_key_cache.lifecycle: Entries expire after 60 seconds; size is bounded; mutation invalidates by generation.
mem.api_key_cache.restart: Starts empty. PostgreSQL api_keys remains authoritative.

mem.cache_routing.overview: Where a prefix-cache copy of a prompt currently lives, plus the two gates that decide whether cache-aware routing participates in a given request.
mem.cache_routing.represents: Per-prefix holder sets with attempt records, donation/hit/miss counters, per-(provider,model) v2 capability rejections and sequence numbers; alongside a deterministic HMAC sampling percentage and a token bucket bounding sidecar plan QPS.
mem.cache_routing.construction: registry.cacheRoutingTracker is built with a TTL and holder cap; registry.cacheActivationGate is built from the configured rollout percentage and max QPS. Both are owned by Registry.
mem.cache_routing.access: Cache-plan admission consults the activation gate; routing reads holder sets to prefer a provider that already has the prefix; provider prefix-cache status/update frames add, refresh and remove holders; stats endpoints read the counters.
mem.cache_routing.concurrency: Each struct has its own mutex. HTTP dispatch goroutines read while provider WebSocket readers write holder state, so the tracker sweeps and bounds itself under the same lock.
mem.cache_routing.lifecycle: Holders expire by TTL and are bounded by holder/entry/attempt caps with heap-ordered eviction; the gate's bucket refills continuously. Both only ever decline cache participation — never ordinary inference.
mem.cache_routing.restart: Starts empty: the fleet re-advertises its prefix caches, and the rollout gate reopens at its configured percentage.

mem.capacity.overview: The coordinator’s current estimate of how much inference work each provider/model can accept and how fast it will run.
mem.capacity.represents: Heartbeat-reported engine slots, token budgets and queue depth plus measured TPS/prefill/TTFT exponential moving averages used by admission and ranking.
mem.capacity.construction: Fields live on Provider and registry calibration/scheduler structures; updates are derived from heartbeats and completed requests.
mem.capacity.access: Heartbeat handling writes advertised capacity; routing snapshots read it; completion paths fold observations into EWMAs; fleet capacity endpoints aggregate snapshots.
mem.capacity.concurrency: Provider fields are read/written under the Provider mutex; calibration maps have their own locks. Updates come from WebSocket readers while HTTP handlers route concurrently.
mem.capacity.lifecycle: Live estimates decay or become irrelevant when a provider disconnects; calibration records are capped/TTL-swept where applicable.
mem.capacity.restart: Live capacity starts empty and is relearned from reconnecting providers; durable reputation may seed part of the routing picture.

mem.challenges.overview: The outstanding attestation challenges a provider connection has been sent but has not yet answered.
mem.challenges.represents: A nonce-keyed map of pendingChallenge records, each holding the nonce, the signed timestamp, when it was sent, and the channel the response is delivered on.
mem.challenges.construction: api.challengeTracker is created per provider WebSocket connection; a record is added when a challenge frame is written and removed when the matching response arrives or the wait times out.
mem.challenges.access: The provider handler adds a challenge before writing it, then blocks on the record's response channel; the WebSocket read loop looks the nonce up and hands the response over. Consecutive timeouts escalate to a forced reconnect.
mem.challenges.concurrency: One mutex guards the pending map. The verifying goroutine and the socket read loop are different goroutines, and the response channel is the handoff between them.
mem.challenges.lifecycle: One challenge round-trip: added on send, removed on response, timeout, or connection teardown. Challenges are issued on registration and then every five minutes.
mem.challenges.restart: Starts empty; reconnecting providers are challenged immediately.

mem.chunk_keys.overview: A memoization layer that avoids repeating X25519 scalar multiplication for every encrypted chunk in one stream.
mem.chunk_keys.represents: A map keyed by the request private-key identity to a peer public key and precomputed 32-byte shared key.
mem.chunk_keys.construction: api.chunkKeyCache is zero-value ready, mutex-protected, and capped at 8,192 entries.
mem.chunk_keys.access: The first chunk derives and inserts; later chunks look up after validating the peer key; terminal cleanup forgets the entry. The cap triggers bounded eviction rather than growth.
mem.chunk_keys.concurrency: One mutex protects lookup/insert/forget because provider WebSocket and stream-terminal paths can touch it concurrently.
mem.chunk_keys.lifecycle: One live request/stream; explicitly forgotten at terminal and bounded globally.
mem.chunk_keys.restart: Starts empty. Derived secrets are intentionally not persisted.

mem.code_attest.overview: APNs code-identity attestation throttling and safe reuse for provider reconnects.
mem.code_attest.represents: Per-device challenge budget, in-flight challenge records, and last successful code-attestation records keyed by secure identity.
mem.code_attest.construction: codeAttestThrottle owns mutex-protected maps and is created with Server; durable rows can seed the reuse cache.
mem.code_attest.access: Provider verification checks fresh reuse, rate-limits APNs pushes, records nonce/challenge, consumes response, persists success, and invalidates on untrust/version mismatch.
mem.code_attest.concurrency: One mutex coordinates provider WebSocket verification goroutines and seeding. Reuse never bypasses fresh nonce/identity gates.
mem.code_attest.lifecycle: Success has a bounded reuse window with jitter; challenge and rate-limit entries expire.
mem.code_attest.restart: Cache is seeded from PostgreSQL code_attestations, but stale rows fall through to live verification.

mem.dispatch.overview: The per-request state of the dispatch loop: which provider is being tried, what has already been tried, and the ranked alternates a retry may fall back to.
mem.dispatch.represents: api.dispatchState carries the immutable request inputs (model, reservation, admission, deadline, cache plan, tool constraints) plus the mutable attempt fields — selected provider, held pre-content chunks, commit flag, last error classification, excluded providers and retry counters. registry.DispatchPlan holds the ranked alternate candidates, a cursor, the set already attempted, and one refresh allowance.
mem.dispatch.construction: runDispatch builds one dispatchState per request; newDispatchPlan builds the plan from the same candidate scan that chose the winner, keeping the lowest-cost non-winner entries without sorting the full pool.
mem.dispatch.access: The dispatch loop reserves the next plan entry, streams, and on a pre-content failure classifies the error and advances the cursor; the speculative-backup goroutine and the capacity-probe collector confirm or demote entries concurrently.
mem.dispatch.concurrency: DispatchPlan.mu is a leaf lock — taken strictly after the registry lock, never the other way — because a request's retry loop, its speculative goroutine and the probe collector all touch the plan. dispatchState is otherwise owned by the request goroutine, with a hedge-advance channel for the speculative handoff.
mem.dispatch.lifecycle: One request. The plan allows a bounded number of alternates and a single full re-scan refresh; capacity-class retries are bounded so a fleet-wide transient cannot storm.
mem.dispatch.restart: Purely per-request; nothing survives the process.

mem.drain.overview: The graceful-shutdown gate that stops new inference admission while counting requests already inside the HTTP pipeline.
mem.drain.represents: A draining boolean/atomic and an in-flight request counter used by readiness, middleware, and shutdown waiting.
mem.drain.construction: Fields belong to Server and are initialized with the server; shutdown flips the gate before waiting for the counter.
mem.drain.access: Middleware increments/decrements around requests. Admission/readiness checks the drain state. Shutdown waits until the count reaches zero or a deadline.
mem.drain.concurrency: Atomic operations avoid a global request lock and make it safe across all HTTP goroutines and the shutdown goroutine.
mem.drain.lifecycle: Process lifetime; once draining begins it remains set until exit.
mem.drain.restart: Always starts non-draining with zero in-flight requests.

mem.exact_cache.overview: Operational state describing exact/prefix-cache availability, not a cache of consumer responses.
mem.exact_cache.represents: Provider cache capability/receipt gauges plus a short TTL snapshot returned by the cache-status API and prompt-sidecar metrics.
mem.exact_cache.construction: Provider receipt state lives in the registry; the API status handler builds and temporarily caches an aggregate snapshot.
mem.exact_cache.access: Provider prefix-cache frames update receipts; routing reads them when preferring reusable context; GET /v1/cache/status aggregates fleet and sidecar state.
mem.exact_cache.concurrency: Provider cache fields use Provider locking; the aggregate status cache has its own mutex/TTL path. WebSocket receipt updates race safely with HTTP inspection.
mem.exact_cache.lifecycle: Receipts are bounded/live evidence and disappear with provider state; the status response has a short TTL.
mem.exact_cache.restart: Starts empty and is relearned from provider frames; it is not restored as authoritative state.

mem.hash_policy.overview: The active allow/deny policy for provider binaries, runtime manifests, templates, and temporarily shed models.
mem.hash_policy.represents: Sets/maps of accepted hashes and reject-model IDs plus booleans indicating whether a policy is configured.
mem.hash_policy.construction: Server maps are populated from active releases/Postgres and optional environment overrides; reject models come from operational configuration.
mem.hash_policy.access: Registration and attestation read hash sets; release/config changes replace maps; request admission checks the reject-model set.
mem.hash_policy.concurrency: Dedicated RWMutexes protect binary/runtime policy maps. Updates replace map snapshots rather than mutating while readers walk them.
mem.hash_policy.lifecycle: Lives until configuration/release changes or process exit.
mem.hash_policy.restart: Rebuilt from active releases and environment configuration; not authoritative independent storage.

mem.media_resolver.overview: The SSRF-safe fetch and rewrite pipeline for HTTPS image/media URLs embedded in consumer requests.
mem.media_resolver.represents: A Resolver with URL policy, DNS/IP validation, global and per-request semaphores, byte budgets, deadlines, and fetched media buffers.
mem.media_resolver.construction: mediafetch.NewResolver is built from environment/config when Server is created.
mem.media_resolver.access: Before dispatch it discovers remote media, validates scheme/host/port and resolved IPs, fetches concurrently within limits, enforces aggregate bytes, and inlines normalized data.
mem.media_resolver.concurrency: A global semaphore bounds fleet-wide outbound fetches; per-request concurrency and a shared byteBudget coordinate readers. Resolver configuration is immutable.
mem.media_resolver.lifecycle: Fetched bytes live only for the request; redirects, deadlines and size caps bound work.
mem.media_resolver.restart: Starts with no fetched media; nothing is persisted.

mem.metrics.overview: Process-local observability accumulated by coordinator code paths.
mem.metrics.represents: Named counters, histogram buckets/samples, gauges and bounded timing/ring data exposed to admin metrics and periodically forwarded to Datadog.
mem.metrics.construction: api.Metrics is constructed with Server and registers gauges after dependencies are wired.
mem.metrics.access: Request/provider/background paths increment or observe metrics; snapshot code copies maps under a read lock; a gauge loop periodically emits point-in-time values.
mem.metrics.concurrency: Metrics.mu is an RWMutex; callers across HTTP, WebSocket, and background goroutines update the same registry safely.
mem.metrics.lifecycle: Process lifetime; bounded histogram/ring structures prevent unbounded growth.
mem.metrics.restart: Resets on restart. Datadog is the durable/remote sink where configured.

mem.model_state.overview: The in-process model catalog and rollout/routing state used to resolve a public model name into provider builds.
mem.model_state.represents: Catalog membership, alias targets, desired/previous rollout builds, provider model inventories, and short-lived pending-load reservations.
mem.model_state.construction: Catalog and aliases are loaded from Postgres into Registry maps; pending model-load entries are created by warm-pool/cold-dispatch planning.
mem.model_state.access: Request admission resolves aliases and checks catalog membership; provider model updates replace advertised inventory; controllers iterate demand and model state to load/prefetch/evict.
mem.model_state.concurrency: Registry and Provider mutexes protect their respective maps. Alias mutations are serialized separately by Server.modelAliasMutationMu before persistence and resync.
mem.model_state.lifecycle: Catalog/aliases persist until changed; pending loads expire after two minutes (or a shorter memory-backoff restamp).
mem.model_state.restart: Catalog and aliases are rebuilt from Postgres. Live provider inventories and pending loads are rebuilt only as providers reconnect/heartbeat.

mem.pending.overview: The rendezvous state connecting one dispatched inference request to asynchronous provider frames.
mem.pending.represents: A PendingRequest per request ID, containing accepted, chunk, completion, and error signaling plus terminal/accounting state. Providers also index their pending requests.
mem.pending.construction: Created immediately before dispatch and attached to the chosen provider; channels are bounded so the provider read loop never depends on an unbounded consumer.
mem.pending.access: The HTTP dispatch loop waits on channels. The provider WebSocket read loop looks up request ID and sends accepted/chunk/terminal events. Cancellation/disconnect closes or removes the record.
mem.pending.concurrency: Provider-local pending maps are protected by the Provider mutex; per-request atomics/once-style terminal gates prevent duplicate closure. WebSocket readers and HTTP stream writers access the same object concurrently.
mem.pending.lifecycle: One request lifetime. It is removed after terminal completion/error/cancel; a late terminal may be parked briefly in the settlement holder.
mem.pending.restart: Starts empty. In-flight streams fail when the process stops.

mem.price_cache.overview: A short-lived in-process cache of per-account model prices, so pricing does not cost a database round trip on every inference request.
mem.price_cache.represents: A map keyed "accountID:model" to input/output micro-USD prices and the time they were read.
mem.price_cache.construction: The map and its RWMutex live on store.PostgresStore and are created with the store; entries are filled lazily on the first lookup for a key.
mem.price_cache.access: GetModelPrice reads under a read lock and, on miss or expiry, queries model_prices and fills under a write lock. SetModelPrice deletes the key after writing the row, so a price change is not shadowed by a stale entry.
mem.price_cache.concurrency: An RWMutex: many request goroutines read concurrently; fills and invalidations take the write lock. A miss is not singleflighted, so a cold key can produce a few duplicate queries.
mem.price_cache.lifecycle: Thirty-second TTL, checked on read, plus explicit invalidation on price mutation. Entries are never swept in the background.
mem.price_cache.restart: Starts empty; every price is re-read from PostgreSQL on first use.

mem.provider_writer.overview: The two-lane serializer in front of each provider WebSocket: one goroutine owns the socket, and every frame the coordinator sends passes through it.
mem.provider_writer.represents: A providerWriter per connection holding the socket, a control channel, a data queue, liveness/deadline atomics and the writer's stop/done channels; plus one providerWriteRequest per frame with its payload, completion channel, handoff channels and an ownership state machine.
mem.provider_writer.construction: Created with the provider connection in the registry; callers submit frames through WriteText / WriteTextControl / EnqueueText rather than touching the socket.
mem.provider_writer.access: Inference request bodies and model commands go to the data lane; attestation challenges, cancels and trust/runtime-status frames go to the control lane and are served with strict priority. A single watchdog goroutine per connection enforces per-frame write deadlines.
mem.provider_writer.concurrency: This is the concurrency boundary itself: the channels serialize many HTTP and scheduler goroutines onto one writer, frame ownership transitions are atomics, and an accept mutex plus a dead flag close the submit path exactly once. FIFO holds within a lane only — ordering across lanes is unspecified, and control priority is non-preemptive.
mem.provider_writer.lifecycle: One provider connection. Frames leave on write completion, cancellation, or the per-frame deadline (up to ~30s for a multi-MiB sealed vision payload).
mem.provider_writer.restart: Recreated on every reconnect; nothing queued survives a disconnect.

mem.queue.overview: A bounded waiting room for inference requests that have no immediately admissible provider.
mem.queue.represents: Per-model FIFO slices of QueuedRequest values, including deadline and wake-up/result channels.
mem.queue.construction: registry.RequestQueue owns map[string][]*QueuedRequest and is built from environment-sized depth and maximum-wait settings.
mem.queue.access: Enqueue appends to one model queue; provider/capacity changes dequeue candidates; cancellation and expiry remove entries; depth/stat methods inspect queues.
mem.queue.concurrency: One RequestQueue.mu mutex serializes all model queues. HTTP request goroutines enqueue/wait while provider and scheduler paths wake or remove entries.
mem.queue.lifecycle: Default maximum depth is 32 per model. Entries leave on assignment, request cancellation, or max-wait timeout.
mem.queue.restart: Starts empty; queued HTTP requests are process-local and are not recoverable.

mem.read_cache.overview: A small shared TTL cache for expensive read-heavy JSON responses.
mem.read_cache.represents: Serialized response bytes keyed by semantic names such as stats, leaderboard, network totals, release and runtime-manifest keys.
mem.read_cache.construction: api.ttlCache owns a map of value + expiry and is created once on Server.
mem.read_cache.access: Handlers perform Get, compute on miss, then Set with endpoint-specific TTL; mutation paths call Invalidate. Expired entries are rejected/removed lazily.
mem.read_cache.concurrency: An RWMutex protects the map. Many HTTP goroutines can read; a miss can still cause duplicate concurrent fills because this is not singleflight.
mem.read_cache.lifecycle: Endpoint TTLs range from short operational snapshots to minutes; invalidation is explicit at mutation boundaries.
mem.read_cache.restart: Starts empty and repopulates from durable/live sources.

mem.registry.overview: The live routing index for provider machines currently connected to the coordinator.
mem.registry.represents: A map from provider ID to a Provider object: its WebSocket writer, advertised models, hardware, trust, health, capacity, pending requests, and routing reputation.
mem.registry.construction: registry.Registry owns map[string]*Provider; each Provider is a long-lived mutable object created when a provider Register frame succeeds.
mem.registry.access: Registration inserts; routing snapshots or scans eligible providers; heartbeat and protocol frames update a provider; disconnect removes it. Fleet views walk the map and then snapshot individual providers.
mem.registry.concurrency: Registry.mu is an RWMutex over membership and shared registry indexes. Each Provider has its own mutex; the socket writer uses bounded channel lanes. Callers must not hold the registry lock while doing network I/O.
mem.registry.lifecycle: Created at coordinator startup. Entries live for one WebSocket session and are evicted on disconnect or stale-heartbeat cleanup.
mem.registry.restart: Starts empty. Persisted provider identity/reputation can be restored when a machine reconnects, but the live socket and routing membership cannot.

mem.route_sink.overview: A best-effort asynchronous write queue that keeps routing telemetry and rejection persistence off inference latency paths.
mem.route_sink.represents: A bounded channel of functions consumed by a fixed worker pool.
mem.route_sink.construction: telemetrySink is created with a fixed capacity and worker count in NewServer.
mem.route_sink.access: Request paths enqueue non-blockingly; workers execute store writes; shutdown drains/stops according to server lifecycle.
mem.route_sink.concurrency: Channel ownership provides concurrency; fixed workers bound DB concurrency and memory. When full, telemetry is dropped rather than blocking inference.
mem.route_sink.lifecycle: Process lifetime; queued work is transient and bounded.
mem.route_sink.restart: Starts empty. Dropped/unflushed best-effort telemetry is not recovered.

mem.rpm.overview: Request-count rate limits that protect consumer, service, financial, telemetry, and per-key entry points.
mem.rpm.represents: Sharded token buckets keyed by account, key, IP, submitter, or financial operation; each bucket tracks tokens and last refill/seen time.
mem.rpm.construction: ratelimit.Limiter instances are constructed from config; per-key overrides use the same bucket mechanism with rates supplied per call.
mem.rpm.access: Middleware/handlers call Allow or Reserve by identity; periodic pruners walk shards and delete idle buckets.
mem.rpm.concurrency: Shard mutexes permit unrelated identities to proceed concurrently while serializing the same bucket. Pruners run in background goroutines.
mem.rpm.lifecycle: Buckets refill continuously and idle buckets are pruned; limits are process-local enforcement state.
mem.rpm.restart: All buckets start full/empty according to limiter semantics; no rate-limit debt is persisted.

mem.service_reservations.overview: Temporary credit reservations for service-account inference so concurrent requests cannot overspend the same backing balance.
mem.service_reservations.represents: A manager tracks reservation IDs/amounts around the durable store’s reserve/finalize operations.
mem.service_reservations.construction: serviceReservationManager is created with Store and reservation config as part of Server.
mem.service_reservations.access: Inference admission reserves before dispatch; terminal settlement finalizes or releases. The manager coordinates retries and idempotent cleanup.
mem.service_reservations.concurrency: Manager state is shared by concurrent HTTP/terminal goroutines and uses its own synchronization plus durable store transaction boundaries.
mem.service_reservations.lifecycle: One inference/accounting lifecycle; cleanup occurs on completion, error, or timeout.
mem.service_reservations.restart: In-memory coordination resets, while the durable ledger/store remains authoritative and reconciles accounting.

mem.settlements.overview: A short grace holder for requests whose consumer stream disappeared before the provider’s terminal usage frame arrived.
mem.settlements.represents: request ID → *registry.PendingRequest, preserving enough accounting context to settle late terminal usage once.
mem.settlements.construction: settlementHolder owns a mutex and pending map and is created with Server.
mem.settlements.access: Consumer cancellation parks a request; provider terminal handling takes/removes it; a grace timer evicts unresolved entries.
mem.settlements.concurrency: One mutex protects the map across HTTP cancellation, provider WebSocket terminal frames, and timer goroutines. Finalization separately guards double counting.
mem.settlements.lifecycle: Only the late-terminal grace window; entries are removed on terminal or timer expiry.
mem.settlements.restart: Starts empty. Any unsettled process-local grace entries are lost, though durable accounting already committed remains.

mem.stored_providers.overview: A startup lookup that reconnects a live provider identity with its durable provider record.
mem.stored_providers.represents: Persisted ProviderRecord values indexed by serial number and Secure Enclave public key.
mem.stored_providers.construction: Registry.LoadStoredProviders reads the store once and Server stores the resulting lookup map.
mem.stored_providers.access: Provider registration looks up serial/SE key to restore account linkage, trust/reputation context and known identity; it is not the live routing registry.
mem.stored_providers.concurrency: Built before serving and then treated as a read-mostly snapshot; provider registration goroutines only read it.
mem.stored_providers.lifecycle: Process-lifetime snapshot. New durable writes do not turn it into live socket state.
mem.stored_providers.restart: Rebuilt from PostgreSQL on every startup.

mem.telemetry_limit.overview: Per-submitter protection for the client telemetry ingestion endpoint.
mem.telemetry_limit.represents: Identity-keyed rate-limit buckets tracking recent submissions.
mem.telemetry_limit.construction: A telemetryLimiter is created with Server from fixed/configured limits.
mem.telemetry_limit.access: The telemetry handler checks the submitter before parsing/forwarding; idle state is reaped according to limiter behavior.
mem.telemetry_limit.concurrency: Internal locking makes concurrent telemetry POSTs for the same or different submitters safe.
mem.telemetry_limit.restart: Starts fresh; Datadog/process logs, not the limiter, are the telemetry record.

mem.token_limits.overview: Token-volume admission limits, separate from requests-per-minute.
mem.token_limits.represents: Per-account and per-key input/output token buckets plus prompt/output estimates used before dispatch and corrected after usage is known.
mem.token_limits.construction: TokenLimiter composes input/output Limiter instances; KeyTokenLimiter holds per-key override buckets.
mem.token_limits.access: Admission peeks/reserves estimated tokens; completion charges/reconciles actual output; pruners remove idle identities.
mem.token_limits.concurrency: Sharded locks and same-account atomic admission prevent concurrent requests from both passing a stale peek. Background pruners run independently.
mem.token_limits.lifecycle: Buckets refill by configured tokens/second and idle records are pruned.
mem.token_limits.restart: Starts fresh; token budget state is not durable billing state.

mem.trust_reuse.overview: A restart-herd suppressor that reuses recent full MDM trust evidence only after fresh identity/runtime proof.
mem.trust_reuse.represents: Secure-Enclave-keyed records of serial, binary hash, posture, verification time and bounded reuse metadata.
mem.trust_reuse.construction: trustReuseCache owns a mutex and record map, is created with Server, and is seeded from provider_trust_reuse rows.
mem.trust_reuse.access: Reconnect checks for a fresh record, still runs live SE challenge/runtime gates, may grant reuse, writes through after full verification, and invalidates on untrust.
mem.trust_reuse.concurrency: One mutex guards reads, writes and seeding across concurrent provider registrations. Cached evidence cannot grant hardware identity by itself.
mem.trust_reuse.lifecycle: Bounded reuse window; stale/mismatched records force full live MicroMDM/APNs verification.
mem.trust_reuse.restart: Rebuilt from PostgreSQL, then revalidated against fresh connection evidence.

mem.ttft.overview: The correction factor between predicted and observed time-to-first-token, learned per model and chip class.
mem.ttft.represents: Sliding ratio windows keyed by (model, chip) and a pending map joining each reserved attempt's raw TTFT prediction to the first-content observation that arrives later.
mem.ttft.construction: registry.ttftCalibrator is a process-wide instance shared by the scheduler (predictions) and the API layer (observations).
mem.ttft.access: Reservation records the raw warm-slot estimate for a request attempt; first content records the actual, folds the clamped ratio into that window, and routing multiplies future estimates by it. Retry-After and TTFT-feasibility decisions read the calibrated value.
mem.ttft.concurrency: An RWMutex: scheduler goroutines read windows while provider read loops record observations. Pending predictions are capped and swept under the same lock.
mem.ttft.lifecycle: Ratios are clamped to a sane band so one pathological sample cannot distort routing; pending predictions expire by sweep when their observation never arrives.
mem.ttft.restart: Starts uncalibrated (ratio 1.0) and relearns from live traffic.

mem.usage_log.overview: A per-consumer log of recent inference usage kept alongside the durable ledger.
mem.usage_log.represents: payments.Ledger's map from consumer ID to UsageEntry records (model, prompt/completion tokens, cost, timestamp). Balances and ledger entries themselves are not here — those are SQL.
mem.usage_log.construction: Created with the Ledger, which otherwise delegates every balance mutation to the store.
mem.usage_log.access: Completion paths append an entry; usage endpoints read a consumer's slice.
mem.usage_log.concurrency: An RWMutex guards the map because many request goroutines append while read endpoints iterate.
mem.usage_log.lifecycle: Process lifetime, append-only per consumer — this is an observability convenience, not the accounting record.
mem.usage_log.restart: Lost on restart. Money is unaffected: balances and ledger entries live in PostgreSQL.

mem.warm_pool.overview: The demand signal and control state behind pre-warming models on providers before requests for them arrive.
mem.warm_pool.represents: Per-model pressure buckets (capacity rejects, TTFT misses, cold dispatches, load successes/failures and a smoothed arrival rate), the latest planning snapshots cached for observability, and a per-model queue-pressure view (depth and oldest age).
mem.warm_pool.construction: registry.warmPoolController owns a warmPoolState, a syncQueuePressure view, a tick mutex and a trigger channel; it is built from WarmPoolConfig and holds the Registry it acts on.
mem.warm_pool.access: Dispatch and queue paths record spill events and queue pressure; the controller ticks, converts demand to a target concurrency by Little's Law and pushes load_model to providers; utilization/stats endpoints read the cached snapshots instead of re-running a planning pass (which has load side effects).
mem.warm_pool.concurrency: Separate locks for the pressure state, the queue view, the cached snapshots and the tick itself — the tick mutex makes planning single-flight while request goroutines keep recording events. Snapshots are cached read-only precisely so observability cannot trigger model loads.
mem.warm_pool.lifecycle: Continuous; arrival rates decay by EWMA and service time is clamped so the demand-to-concurrency conversion cannot run away. An observe-only mode records without acting.
mem.warm_pool.restart: Starts with no pressure history and relearns from live spill events.

mem.x25519.overview: The coordinator side of end-to-end encrypted inference transport.
mem.x25519.represents: A 32-byte X25519 private/public key pair used to derive per-provider/per-request shared keys; plaintext prompts remain hidden from the coordinator in sealed flows.
mem.x25519.construction: Generated or loaded during Server construction/configuration and exposed through the encryption-key endpoint as public material only.
mem.x25519.access: Dispatch/decryption paths read the private key to derive NaCl box shared keys; consumers/providers use the public key in the wire contract.
mem.x25519.concurrency: The key is immutable after initialization, so concurrent request goroutines read it without mutation.
mem.x25519.lifecycle: Server/session lifetime according to deployment key configuration.
mem.x25519.restart: If generated in memory it rotates on restart; if supplied by deployment configuration it is reloaded. Per-request derived keys are never durable.

mem.zombie_cancel.overview: A bounded cancel retransmission throttle for streams that keep producing chunks after the consumer is gone.
mem.zombie_cancel.represents: request ID → last cancel time, used to avoid flooding a provider socket with repeated cancel frames.
mem.zombie_cancel.construction: zombieStreamCanceller owns a mutex-protected timestamp map.
mem.zombie_cancel.access: Late chunk handling asks whether another cancel is allowed; allowed sends update the timestamp; cleanup/expiry removes old request IDs.
mem.zombie_cancel.concurrency: The mutex coordinates provider read-loop events and stream cleanup.
mem.zombie_cancel.lifecycle: One short throttle window per request; stale entries are removed/bounded.
mem.zombie_cancel.restart: Starts empty; cancellation hints are not durable.

pg.api_keys.represents: Durable api keys records used by the coordinator. This node represents SQL rows and indexes—not a Go object or cache.
pg.api_keys.construction: Declared and migrated by PostgresStore; handlers reach it through typed coordinator/store methods.
pg.api_keys.access: R/W/RW badges show whether each API namespace selects, mutates, or does both. “Used by” lists the exact endpoint handlers associated with this table.
pg.api_keys.concurrency: Concurrency is owned by the typed client/store or by the coordinator object named here; request handlers do not mutate an unguarded global value.
pg.api_keys.lifecycle: Rows survive process restarts; append-only histories and mutable current-state rows are both managed transactionally by PostgreSQL.
pg.api_keys.restart: See the category durability rule; durable truth is reloaded, external/protocol state is re-established.

mdm.client.represents: Correlation state between a command the coordinator sent to MicroMDM and the check-in that answers it.

mdm.client.access: The MDM webhook endpoint resolves waiters; the background verification scheduler registers them. A lost webhook expires the waiter rather than blocking a request.
mdm.client.concurrency: Guarded by the client's own mutex; handlers never touch the maps directly.
mdm.client.lifecycle: Per-attempt entries with timeouts; nothing survives a restart.

roles.title: Customer dashboard
roles.summary: An account owner uses an interactive Privy session for account, billing, key-management, and preference operations. A leaked API key cannot mint more keys.
roles.custody: Privy manages the interactive session. The pinned console explicitly stores the active inference API key in browser localStorage in clear text and removes it on logout.

roles.title: Customer API client
roles.summary: An application sends inference and model requests with an account-scoped API key. Per-key limits and spend attribution travel with the authenticated key record.
roles.custody: Raw key belongs in the client secret store; the coordinator retains only a SHA-256 hash and metadata.

roles.title: Upstream router
roles.summary: A trusted aggregator uses the same bearer-key plane as ordinary API clients, with router-specific telemetry and routing behavior.
roles.custody: Raw key belongs in the router secret manager; only the key hash and account metadata are durable server-side.

roles.title: Provider operator
roles.summary: The machine owner starts the device authorization flow, approves it in a browser, and receives a provider token linking that machine to an account.
roles.custody: The provider token is written to ~/.darkbloom/auth_token with mode 0600.

roles.title: Provider node
roles.summary: A Swift provider opens the fleet WebSocket, presents its account-link token during registration, and proves machine identity/posture through attestation.
roles.custody: Account token: owner-only file. Device private key: Secure Enclave with a Keychain reference; it is not exported.

roles.title: Provider dashboard
roles.summary: An authenticated provider owner reads earnings, payout, trust, and machine state through account-scoped endpoints.
roles.custody: Normally an interactive Privy browser session. The earnings UI may fall back to the browser localStorage API key; low-volume general-bearer routes can also resolve an active provider token.

roles.title: Administrator
roles.summary: Administrators use either a configured Privy-admin identity or the break-glass administrator bearer key. Authentication is followed by an explicit admin authorization check.
roles.custody: Admin key is generated once, kept in deployment Secret Manager/KMS, and injected into the coordinator environment. The OTP-based admin CLI stores its Privy token at ~/.darkbloom/admin_token with mode 0600; an admin-key override is read from process environment.

roles.title: Model publisher / CI
roles.summary: Publishing automation registers and promotes model artifacts with a narrow publishing credential rather than broad customer credentials.
roles.custody: Raw key belongs in the CI secret store. Durable publishing keys are SHA-256 hashed in PostgreSQL; a bootstrap key may be injected via environment.

roles.title: Release CI
roles.summary: GitHub Actions registers provider binary releases with a credential scoped to POST /v1/releases.
roles.custody: The same value is held in the GitHub environment secret and deployment Secret Manager, then injected into coordinator memory through its environment.

roles.title: Stripe
roles.summary: Stripe calls billing webhooks. The coordinator does not trust source IP or a user bearer; it verifies each signed payload against the endpoint-specific webhook secret.
roles.custody: Stripe holds the signing side; matching webhook secrets are copied from Stripe into deployment Secret Manager and injected into the coordinator environment.

roles.title: MicroMDM
roles.summary: MicroMDM posts device command results to the coordinator. A shared webhook token is defense in depth on top of mandatory CommandUUID correlation.
roles.custody: Both daemons receive matching values from the deployment environment; the callback token stays on localhost and is placed in the generated webhook URL.

roles.title: Infrastructure automation
roles.summary: Health, metrics, and operational probes primarily use public/read-only surfaces or deployment-scoped access according to the endpoint.
roles.custody: No credential for the classified public probes; network policy and deployment controls remain separate from application authentication.

roles.title: Public / auditor
roles.summary: Public catalog, status, installation, and audit-style endpoints intentionally expose bounded non-secret information.
roles.custody: No application credential. Public does not mean unrestricted data: each handler defines a deliberately bounded response.

roles.title: Coordinator service
roles.summary: The coordinator validates inbound identities and also holds narrowly scoped credentials for outbound calls to Privy, Stripe, and MicroMDM.
roles.custody: Service credentials come from deployment Secret Manager/KMS into environment variables or an explicitly configured file; they are not client bearer credentials.

credentials.title: Customer API key
credentials.holder: Customer API client / dashboard / upstream router
credentials.clientStorage: Machine integrations use a client-owned secret manager or environment (exact store is external). The pinned customer/provider console stores its active inference key in browser localStorage in clear text.
credentials.serverStorage: PostgreSQL api_keys.key_hash (SHA-256) plus prefix, owner, limits, expiry, and status; positive auth results also enter a short TTL in-memory cache keyed by the presented bearer.
credentials.validation: requireAuth resolves the bearer through AuthenticateKey, then enforces disable/expiry and binds account/key metadata into request context.
credentials.lifetime: No default expiry; optional expires_at plus disable, delete, and atomic rotation. Raw material is returned at issuance/rotation and is not recoverable from the database.

credentials.title: Privy access token
credentials.holder: Interactive customer, provider owner, or administrator
credentials.clientStorage: Privy client/session layer in the dashboard or browser. Exact browser persistence is outside this repository and should not be inferred.
credentials.serverStorage: The access token is not persisted by the coordinator. It keeps the Privy verification public key and maps the verified DID to a users row.
credentials.validation: Local ES256 verification checks issuer privy.io, audience/app ID, signature, and claims; sensitive key-management routes reject non-Privy bearers.
credentials.lifetime: Controlled by Privy token claims/session policy.

credentials.title: Device authorization code
credentials.holder: Provider CLI temporarily; user holds the human-readable approval code
credentials.clientStorage: Provider process memory while polling. The approved long-lived token replaces it; the Swift flow does not persist the device_code.
credentials.serverStorage: PostgreSQL device_codes currently stores device_code and user_code in plaintext until expiry/status transition.
credentials.validation: The browser approval leg requires interactive Privy authentication; the polling leg proves possession of device_code.
credentials.lifetime: 15-minute RFC 8628-style exchange with a recommended 5-second poll interval. At this revision an approved record is not consumed, so repeated polling before expiry can mint additional provider tokens.

credentials.title: Provider account-link token
credentials.clientStorage: Canonical ~/.darkbloom/auth_token, owner read/write only (0600); an override exists for isolated test harnesses.
credentials.serverStorage: PostgreSQL provider_tokens.token_hash (SHA-256), account ID, label, active flag, and creation time.
credentials.validation: Registration resolves AuthToken to an active provider-token row and stamps the resulting account ID; general bearer middleware can also resolve it for account-scoped low-volume calls.
credentials.lifetime: No fixed expiry column. Server-side active/revocation state exists, but darkbloom logout at this revision only deletes the local file and does not revoke the stored token.

credentials.title: Provider attestation identity
credentials.clientStorage: Private key operations stay in Secure Enclave; the persistent reference and related material use the data-protection Keychain/access group.
credentials.serverStorage: Coordinator stores bounded attestation/trust results and public identity/correlation state, not the device private key.
credentials.validation: Fresh coordinator nonce is signed by the device and combined with runtime, MDM, and optional APNs code-identity checks before trust/routing upgrades.
credentials.lifetime: Persistent device identity; trust evidence is refreshed and bounded independently.

credentials.title: Administrator key
credentials.clientStorage: Deployment Secret Manager/KMS; admin scripts may receive it through EIGENINFERENCE_ADMIN_KEY in a tightly scoped process environment.
credentials.serverStorage: Injected as EIGENINFERENCE_ADMIN_KEY and held in coordinator memory; deployment may also seed its hashed API-key form for general auth compatibility.
credentials.validation: Constant-time compare in requireAuth, followed by endpoint-specific administrator authorization. A configured Privy-admin identity is the non-key alternative.
credentials.lifetime: Generated once in documented dev wiring; rotate by replacing the deployment secret and clients together.

credentials.title: Model publishing key
credentials.clientStorage: CI secret store (exact platform/location is deployment-specific). A bootstrap value may come from MODEL_REGISTRY_PUBLISHING_KEY.
credentials.serverStorage: Durable keys are SHA-256 hashed in PostgreSQL publishing_api_keys. Bootstrap and administrator alternatives are environment/in-memory values.
credentials.validation: Publishing handlers accept a matching active hashed publishing key, the bootstrap environment key, or the administrator key.
credentials.lifetime: Durable keys can be disabled/rotated; bootstrap lifetime follows deployment secret rotation.

credentials.title: Release registration key
credentials.clientStorage: GitHub Actions secrets DEV_RELEASE_KEY / PROD_RELEASE_KEY, with legacy RELEASE_KEY fallback.
credentials.serverStorage: Deployment Secret Manager/KMS → EIGENINFERENCE_RELEASE_KEY → coordinator memory; not stored in an application table.
credentials.validation: Constant-time comparison inside POST /v1/releases; it does not grant administrator access.
credentials.lifetime: No expiry or dual-key overlap is evident; rotate the GitHub and deployment copies together, then restart the coordinator.

credentials.title: Stripe webhook signature
credentials.clientStorage: Stripe owns the signing system; no customer/browser key is involved.
credentials.serverStorage: Endpoint-specific webhook secrets live in deployment Secret Manager/KMS and are injected as EIGENINFERENCE_STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET and ...CONNECT_WEBHOOK_SECRET.
credentials.validation: Coordinator verifies Stripe-Signature against the raw payload and the matching endpoint secret before any billing state transition.
credentials.lifetime: Per-request signature; webhook secret rotates through Stripe and deployment configuration.

credentials.title: MicroMDM webhook token
credentials.clientStorage: When configured, start.sh injects it into MicroMDM’s localhost command-webhook URL as ?token= because the daemon cannot set a header. Actual deployment presence is uncertain.
credentials.serverStorage: EIGENINFERENCE_MDM_WEBHOOK_SECRET in environment and coordinator memory. The visible dev refresh script does not provision it.
credentials.validation: Constant-time token comparison occurs before reading the body; a one-shot, unexpired CommandUUID from a coordinator-issued command is still mandatory.
credentials.lifetime: Optional deployment-scoped secret with no overlap rotation. CommandUUID correlation lasts 30 minutes and is consumed once.

credentials.title: MicroMDM API key
credentials.clientStorage: Not a user credential. Both local services receive byte-identical values from deployment configuration.
credentials.serverStorage: Deployment Secret Manager/KMS → MICROMDM_API_KEY and EIGENINFERENCE_MDM_API_KEY environment variables.
credentials.validation: MicroMDM validates coordinator API calls; mismatch makes device/trust lookups fail.
credentials.lifetime: Deployment-scoped; rotate both service configurations atomically.

credentials.title: Privy application secret + verification key
credentials.serverStorage: Secret Manager/KMS → EIGENINFERENCE_PRIVY_APP_SECRET; verification public key comes from env or EIGENINFERENCE_PRIVY_VERIFICATION_KEY_FILE.
credentials.validation: Public key verifies inbound ES256 tokens; app secret authenticates coordinator REST calls used to fetch user details/OTP operations.
credentials.lifetime: Rotated in Privy and deployment configuration; public verifier material is not itself secret.

credentials.title: Stripe secret API key
credentials.clientStorage: Not distributed to browsers or webhook callers.
credentials.serverStorage: Deployment Secret Manager/KMS → EIGENINFERENCE_STRIPE_SECRET_KEY → coordinator process environment/memory.
credentials.validation: Stripe authenticates coordinator-created checkout, Connect, transfer, and dashboard API requests. It is distinct from webhook verification secrets.
credentials.lifetime: Rotated through Stripe and deployment configuration.

mem.media_resolver.reason: The inference path consults the resolver and may fetch/cache resolved remote media before dispatch.

authRules.detail: Provider WebSocket protocol authentication: provider token/registration identity plus coordinator trust and attestation checks.
Possession of the short-lived device_code secret issued by the coordinator.
No prior authentication; starts Privy email OTP for a configured administrator account.
Possession and successful verification of the Privy email OTP; returns an access token.
No bearer token; lookup is scoped by the supplied provider address.
No authentication. Compatibility tombstone always returns HTTP 410 before reading the body.
No user bearer token. Stripe-Signature is verified against the configured webhook secret before processing.
MicroMDM callback authentication, using the configured webhook shared secret when enabled and correlated command/device state.
Model publishing key, bootstrap publishing key, or configured administrator key, validated inside the publishing handler.
Scoped release-registration bearer key intended for release automation.
Authorization: Bearer with an interactive Privy access token. ES256 JWT verification is local; API keys and provider tokens are rejected.
General bearer authentication plus an administrator authorization check (configured admin key or Privy-authenticated configured administrator).
Authorization: Bearer. requireAuth accepts a Privy JWT, administrator key, API key, or active provider token; handler authorization may narrow this further.
Handler-internal administrator gate: configured admin bearer key or a Privy-authenticated configured administrator.
No endpoint authentication. Any network client can call it.

GET /api/version.description: Returns the current provider software version policy for update checks.

GET /health.description: Returns coordinator liveness and the current connected-provider count.

GET /install.sh.description: Returns a generated provider installation shell script with the coordinator base URL substituted.

GET /readyz.description: Readiness probe that returns unavailable while the coordinator is draining.

ANY /v1/.description: Returns a structured OpenAI-style JSON 404 for otherwise unimplemented /v1 routes.
ANY /v1/.details: Catch-all only; more-specific registered routes always win.

POST /v1/admin/auth/init.description: Starts admin CLI authentication by sending a Privy email OTP to an allowlisted administrator.

POST /v1/admin/auth/verify.description: Verifies the admin OTP and returns an administrator session token.

GET /v1/admin/base-rewards.description: Returns base-reward settlement status and aggregates.

POST /v1/admin/credit.description: Credits an account ledger as an administrative adjustment.

POST /v1/admin/drain.description: Enters graceful drain mode so new inference dispatches stop before restart.

POST /v1/admin/invite-codes.description: Creates an administrator-issued invite code and credit policy.

GET /v1/admin/log-reports/{id}.description: Retrieves one provider log report for administrators.

GET /v1/admin/metrics.description: Returns an administrator-only coordinator metrics snapshot in JSON or Prometheus form.

GET /v1/admin/models/aliases.description: Lists standard public model aliases and rollout pointers.

POST /v1/admin/models/aliases.description: Creates or updates a stable public model alias, desired build, fallback build, and provider desired-state fan-out.

DELETE /v1/admin/models/aliases/{aliasID.description: Deletes a standard model alias and pushes the revised desired-model state to providers.

GET /v1/admin/models/openrouter-aliases.description: Lists model aliases exposed only in the OpenRouter feed.

POST /v1/admin/models/openrouter-aliases.description: Creates or replaces an OpenRouter-only alias with marketplace and Hugging Face identities.

POST /v1/admin/models/register.description: Registers and verifies a manifest-backed model version, pricing, files, and optional promotion.

POST /v1/admin/models/.description: Applies a publishing-key-authorized action to one model: promote, status, runtime parameters, capabilities, deprecation date, OpenRouter slug, or Hugging Face ID.
POST /v1/admin/models/.details: Effective path: /v1/admin/models/{modelID}/{action}. Actions: promote, status, runtime-parameters, capabilities, deprecation, openrouter-slug, hugging-face-id.

PUT /v1/admin/pricing.description: Sets platform default pricing for a model.

GET /v1/admin/rejections.description: Browses rejected-request metadata with reason, model, and counterfactual-capacity filters.
GET /v1/admin/rejections.details: Query: reason, model, could_have_served=true|false, since, limit.

GET /v1/admin/rejections/export.description: Streams rejected-request metadata as CSV or NDJSON.
GET /v1/admin/rejections/export.details: Same rejection filters plus format=csv|ndjson; default CSV.

POST /v1/admin/reward.description: Issues an administrative reward to an account or provider.

GET /v1/admin/routes.description: Browses metadata-only routing-decision records with filters and bounded pagination.
GET /v1/admin/routes.details: Query: provider, model, outcome, final_status, since, limit. since accepts a Go duration or RFC3339; default 24h.

GET /v1/admin/routes/export.description: Streams routing-decision metadata as CSV or NDJSON for calibration and offline analysis.
GET /v1/admin/routes/export.details: Same route filters plus format=csv|ndjson; default CSV. Store reads remain hard-capped.

GET /v1/admin/state-export.description: Streams a gated, encrypted export of sealed coordinator state for disaster recovery.
GET /v1/admin/state-export.details: Requires feature enablement, administrator authorization, and encrypted output protection.

PUT /v1/admin/users/platform-fee.description: Sets a per-account platform fee override.

GET /v1/admin/utilization.description: Returns administrator-only demand, capacity, and utilization breakdowns.

DELETE /v1/auth/keys.description: Revokes the account’s primary API key.

POST /v1/auth/keys.description: Creates the account’s primary API key from an interactive user session.

GET /v1/billing/methods.description: Lists billing and payout methods supported by the coordinator.

DELETE /v1/billing/stripe/account.description: Detaches the interactive user’s Stripe Connect account when safe.

POST /v1/billing/stripe/connect/webhook.description: Consumes and verifies Stripe Connect account and payout webhooks.

POST /v1/billing/stripe/create-session.description: Creates a Stripe checkout session for funding an account.

POST /v1/billing/stripe/dashboard.description: Creates a short-lived Stripe Express dashboard link.

POST /v1/billing/stripe/onboard.description: Starts Stripe Connect Express onboarding for provider payouts.

GET /v1/billing/stripe/session.description: Returns the state of a Stripe funding checkout session.

GET /v1/billing/stripe/status.description: Returns Stripe Connect onboarding and payout readiness.

POST /v1/billing/stripe/webhook.description: Consumes and verifies Stripe payment webhooks to credit funded balances.

GET /v1/billing/wallet/balance.description: Returns the authenticated billing wallet balance.

POST /v1/billing/withdraw/stripe.description: Creates a withdrawal from provider earnings through Stripe Connect.

GET /v1/cache/status.description: Reports aggregate prompt-sidecar and exact-prefix-cache rollout health without provider, model, or account identities.
GET /v1/cache/status.details: Response includes sidecar enabled/running/ready, generation, restart count, preloaded contracts, and rollout mode.

POST /v1/chat/completions.description: Dispatches an OpenAI Chat Completions or Responses request through provider selection and streams or returns the result.
POST /v1/chat/completions.details: Body: OpenAI chat schema. Supports streaming. Middleware: drain gate, API auth, account rate limit, optional sealed transport.

POST /v1/completions.description: Dispatches an OpenAI-compatible legacy text completion request.
POST /v1/completions.details: Body: legacy prompt/completion schema. Supports streaming.

POST /v1/device/approve.description: Approves a device code from an interactive user session and links the provider to that account.

POST /v1/device/code.description: Starts the provider device-authorization flow and returns a short user code plus polling secret.

POST /v1/device/token.description: Polls the device-authorization flow and returns a provider linking token after approval.
POST /v1/device/token.details: The device_code is itself the polling credential until approval or expiry.

GET /v1/encryption-key.description: Publishes the coordinator X25519 public key for optional sender-to-coordinator request encryption.

POST /v1/enroll.description: Generates a per-device Apple MDM enrollment profile.

POST /v1/invite/redeem.description: Redeems an invite code and credits the authenticated account.

GET /v1/key.description: Returns OpenRouter-shaped metadata for the API key making the request.

GET /v1/keys.description: Lists the interactive user’s named API keys and limits.

POST /v1/keys.description: Creates a named, individually limited API key.

GET /v1/keys/{id}.description: Returns one owned API key’s metadata; secret material is not re-disclosed.

PATCH /v1/keys/{id}.description: Updates one owned API key’s name, limits, or enabled state.

POST /v1/keys/{id}/rotate.description: Rotates an owned API key and returns the replacement secret once.

GET /v1/leaderboard.description: Returns a pseudonymized provider leaderboard by earnings, tokens, or completed jobs.

POST /v1/mdm/webhook.description: Accepts MicroMDM command-result webhooks used for provider device enrollment and attestation.

GET /v1/me/providers.description: Lists providers owned by the interactive user.

DELETE /v1/me/providers/{id}.description: Hard-deletes an owned retired or offline provider record after ownership checks.

GET /v1/me/self-route-models.description: Lists alias-aware live model IDs owned by the user for configuring self-route-only API keys.

GET /v1/me/summary.description: Returns the interactive user’s provider, balance, earnings, and account summary.

POST /v1/messages.description: Dispatches an Anthropic Messages-compatible request and translates the provider stream.
POST /v1/messages.details: Body: Anthropic Messages schema. Supports streaming.

GET /v1/models.description: Lists models available to the calling key, including live routing and pricing metadata.

GET /v1/models/capacity.description: Returns a short-lived per-model capacity snapshot for upstream routers.
GET /v1/models/capacity.details: Designed for polling; cache lifetime is approximately 2 seconds and draining state is surfaced.

GET /v1/models/catalog.description: Returns the public active model registry with metadata and platform pricing.

GET /v1/models/catalog/manifest/.description: Returns the verified file manifest for one catalog model.
GET /v1/models/catalog/manifest/.details: Effective path: /v1/models/catalog/manifest/{id}; the handler parses the suffix after the registered subtree.

GET /v1/models/catalog/.description: Returns one public model catalog record.
GET /v1/models/catalog/.details: Effective path: /v1/models/catalog/{id}; the exact /catalog route takes precedence.

GET /v1/models/openrouter.description: Returns a pure OpenRouter-compatible model feed without Darkbloom-specific metadata.

GET /v1/models/{id...}.description: Retrieves one model by a possibly slashed model ID.
GET /v1/models/{id...}.details: The Go 1.22 remainder wildcard permits slashed Hugging Face-style model IDs.

GET /v1/network/series.description: Returns compact complete-bucket request and token time series for a bounded lookback window.
GET /v1/network/series.details: Query: window=30m|24h|7d|30d. Buckets range from 1 minute to 12 hours; responses are cached for 1 minute.

GET /v1/network/totals.description: Returns cached network-wide aggregate usage and capacity totals.

GET /v1/payments/balance.description: Returns the authenticated account’s balance ledger summary.

GET /v1/payments/usage.description: Returns usage records and token/cost aggregates for the authenticated account.

DELETE /v1/pricing.description: Removes provider-specific pricing and restores platform defaults.

GET /v1/pricing.description: Returns public platform pricing and the caller’s applicable provider overrides when available.

PUT /v1/pricing.description: Sets authenticated provider-specific input and output token prices.

GET /v1/provider/account-earnings.description: Returns account-scoped provider earnings and payout totals.

GET /v1/provider/earnings.description: Returns earnings for a provider identity supplied by the caller.

POST /v1/provider/log-report.description: Uploads an explicit provider log report under authenticated account scope.

GET /v1/providers/attestation.description: Publishes independently verifiable provider hardware and Apple attestation evidence.

POST /v1/referral/apply.description: Applies a referral code to the authenticated account.

GET /v1/referral/info.description: Returns the account’s referral relationship and code information.

POST /v1/referral/register.description: Creates or returns the account’s referral code.

GET /v1/referral/stats.description: Returns referral counts, credits, and reward statistics.

POST /v1/releases.description: Registers a signed provider release and its download metadata.
POST /v1/releases.details: Authorization: scoped release registration key; intended for CI publishing.

GET /v1/releases/latest.description: Returns the latest active provider release for installers and update checks.

POST /v1/responses.description: Dispatches an OpenAI Responses API request through the same routing pipeline as chat completions.
POST /v1/responses.details: Body: OpenAI Responses schema; the shared handler auto-detects input versus messages. Supports streaming.

GET /v1/runtime/manifest.description: Returns approved provider runtime hashes and runtime policy.

GET /v1/stats.description: Returns public network and provider hardware statistics, geospatial buckets, traffic flows, tokens, and power estimates.
GET /v1/stats.details: Public but privacy-bucketed where appropriate; cached for approximately 60 seconds.

POST /v1/telemetry/events.description: Compatibility tombstone: returns HTTP 410 before reading the body; client-owned telemetry ingestion is disabled.
POST /v1/telemetry/events.details: Deliberately retained for mixed-version clients but always responds Gone; coordinator-owned operational telemetry is separate.

GET /ws/provider.description: Upgrades to the authenticated provider control-plane WebSocket used for registration, heartbeats, inference relay, and receipts.
